result.title: Selective Monocular Precession Estimation under Geometric and Evaluation Ambiguity: An Auditable Synthetic Study with ORBIT-SCOUT
result.comment: 29 pages, 4 figures and 7 tables; extended narrative review and ancillary code/data for descriptive arithmetic and physical-metric reproduction
result.summary: Monocular observations of a tumbling object can support a precise fitted trajectory without establishing that the recovered physical axis is correct. We study this distinction for elongated, approximately cylindrical targets observed by a calibrated stationary camera. ORBIT-SCOUT couples image-derived line and rim geometry to constant-cone and torque-free triaxial trajectory families, then returns a linked momentum-axis and mean-precession-rate estimate only when numerical, geometric, temporal and competing-hypothesis checks pass. We describe the measurement objective, selection policy and limitations, and situate them within spacecraft pose estimation, unknown-target reconstruction, rigid-body identification and selective prediction. An internally preregistered population of 96 new synthetic scenes was processed in two cold passes, retaining all 192 attempts. In the primary pass, 38 scenes produced jointly correct estimates, none produced an incorrect estimate, 57 were withheld and one execution was incomplete. Correct coverage on the 64 supported scenes was 25/64. Ninety-five repeated pairs were scientifically equivalent under a frozen comparison policy; the remaining pair was incomplete. The registered coverage, failure-free execution and all-case repeatability targets were not met. Historical audits also exposed an overly permissive axis metric and motion-dependent acquisition cadence. The contribution is a documented measurement-to-decision implementation and a failure-preserving evaluation case study, not a new rigid-body theory or evidence of state-of-the-art accuracy. Zero observed errors does not establish calibrated risk, and conditional temporal checks do not remove shared image-feature bias. Real-image transfer and external reproduction remain open.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究细长近圆柱形翻滚目标的单目进动估计问题，提出 ORBIT-SCOUT：把图像线段与轮廓几何同恒定锥面、无扭矩三轴轨迹族耦合，仅在数值、几何、时序与竞争假设检查全部通过时才输出动量轴与平均进动率，并在 96 个合成场景、两轮冷处理的可审计设置下报告全部尝试（含被扣留与执行不完整案例）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多重检查门控 + 拒绝输出」的选择性预测流程与保留失败的评估设计，可供核查 LVR 中的 STOP 决策、证据充分性判定及「零观测错误≠校准风险」的解释；但对象是航天器姿态测量，与 latent 推理表示无直接联系。
